mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS on 20-day forward returns falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window or average 20-day return during rate declines is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.0% in a 3-month window, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 20-day forward return when UNRATE > 4.0% is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or signal triggers in >40% of sample without negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown in both housing and manufacturing sectors, reducing corporate revenue growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Interaction term (HOUST * INDPRO) has Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window or negative returns not observed when both series decline simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.5%), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days as higher interest rates dampen economic activity and equity valuations.
failure_condition: Average 60-day forward return during FEDFUNDS > 2.5% is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or negative returns occur in <60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for PAYEMS on 5-day forward returns falls below 0.03 in any 2-year rolling window or average 5-day return during payroll increases is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1200.0 thousand units, it indicates a weakening in the housing sector that reduces consumer confidence and corporate investment, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 20-day forward return when HOUST < 1200.0 is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or signal triggers in >40% of sample without negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals an overheating economy that prompts aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Interaction term (CPIAUCSL * UNRATE) has Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window or negative returns not observed when CPIAUCSL rises and UNRATE falls simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions (when industrial production growth falls below 1.0% annually), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days as supply-side constraints limit economic growth and corporate margins.
failure_condition: Average 60-day forward return during INDPRO growth < 1.0% is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or negative returns occur in <60% of such periods.
